trail_notes: 'trail' lists the old value and the evidence for the change. After the ask session the runner checks whether each string is still in a memory note, and, for arms with a git history, whether it is in the note files or in that history. Added in version 3; version 3 also accepts "isn't live" for flag-rollback's premise question.
notes: Synthetic scenarios written for receipts-wiki, modelled on STALE (arXiv:2605.06527) and Supersede (arXiv:2606.27472). Dates are absolute so the eval measures update handling, not date conversion. Question kinds: current (latest value), premise (question built on a stale premise), retained (a fact the correction must not change), history (what changed and why). 'seeded' lists strings that must be in a memory note after the teach session; when they are missing, the arm had nothing to correct and its result does not measure update handling. Version 2 (2026-09-14): ttl-explicit no longer cites a config commit, because plain auto memory declined to save a fact it could read from git, in both smoke runs.

scenarios.teach: Please save this to your memory for future sessions: our quotes API response cache TTL is 60 minutes. The API team agreed on that value on 2026-08-01.
scenarios.correct: Correction, please update your memory: on 2026-09-02 we cut the quotes API cache TTL from 60 to 5 minutes, because 14 of 200 sampled quotes were stale (query q_8812).

questions.q: What is the quotes API cache TTL now?
Given that the quotes cache TTL is still 60 minutes, what is the longest a quote can be stale?
What was the TTL before the change, and why was it changed?
